title: InferOps V1 test inventory
description: Every pytest module in this repository, the test layer it belongs to, the lane that layer runs in, and the published claim each one protects. It is the answer to 'which claim does this suite defend', asked of every suite rather than of the ones somebody remembered. A module absent from this file, a module whose layer disagrees with the strategy, a module naming a claim its layer does not support, and a claim no module names are each a failure in tests/testing/test_test_inventory.py. It records coverage, not certification: what a passing result may be used to claim is decided by the layer's evidence class in test-strategy.v1alpha1.json and by nothing here.

modules.protects: Every serving-adapter implementation this repository ships is discovered rather than listed, and each one is held to the shared conformance suite; the adapter kinds the domain accepts, the kinds the adapters declare, and the kinds the API can compose are one vocabulary.
The adapter for the selected runtime against the shared conformance suite and its own obligations, over a transport the suite controls.
The strings the mock and the real adapter must agree on, compared rather than trusted, so that the two cannot describe the same concept differently.
The capability declaration, and the rule that a declared presence needs a record behind it rather than an assumption.
Configuration translation in both directions between platform values and runtime arguments, and what it refuses to translate.
The request the adapter sends, the response it reads, and the mapping from a runtime condition to a canonical error.
What the adapter reports about the runtime and the model, and which parts of that are configured rather than observed.
Every pinned image digest, model revision, and artifact hash in the adapter, compared against the committed record that decided it.
modules.note: No published claim covers this. It checks that a constant copied out of an accepted decision still matches its source; the claim that the artifact matches its published hash is certified by the real-runtime layer, which this module cannot reach and does not attempt to.

modules.protects: Readiness is false until the runtime says otherwise and false again if it stops saying so, which is what separates a loading runtime from a broken one.
The runtime settings the operator supplies: what they refuse, and the values they refuse to invent a default for.
The transport seam the adapter is handed: what it publishes, what it refuses to carry, and how an unreachable runtime arrives at the adapter.
What the mock owes beyond protocol conformance: determinism, injected canonical failures, and the safeguards that stop a mock transcript naming a real model.
The committed mock adapter against every obligation the serving protocol publishes, inherited rather than copied.
Which adapter a deployment serves is read from configuration and never defaulted, and a real selection with missing settings is refused rather than answered with a mock.

Every condition the API can refuse on is provoked or recorded unreachable, and each refusal is held to the code, flag, status, and identifier the published table declares; every published route is served, echoes the caller's correlation identifier, and names the adapter kind behind the deployment.
The API end to end against the committed mock adapter: the success path and each failure the mock can be driven into.
The canonical error body at every refusal site, why retryability follows the condition rather than the code, and the rule that an adapter's own words stop at this edge.
Liveness, readiness, the model list, and the metrics endpoint that publishes no series, each carrying the adapter kind and no runtime detail.
The inference endpoint end to end against the mock adapter: the borrowed response shape, the extension member, and the identifiers on both.
Starting, serving, draining, and stopping in that order: readiness goes false while work is still in flight, and the adapter is released only after the drain.
modules.note: No published claim covers the lifecycle. ADR 0010 chose graceful drain over a remote-stop endpoint and the claim matrix names no claim about it; the suite exists because the order is the property and an out-of-order drain is invisible in every other suite.

modules.protects: What the API actually emits, read off a running application rather than off a document: every request counted including the ones that failed, the in-flight gauge returning to zero on a refusal, a timeout separated from an error, tokens counted only where the adapter reported them, and no prompt, completion, or adapter message in any record or series.

The readiness rule ADR 0020 decided: the status of the readiness path follows the API lifecycle and not the selected adapter, the adapter's answer is a separate member of the body, the ask is bounded, and an inference request to a ready API with an unavailable runtime receives the canonical dependency error. The real adapter type runs over a controlled transport.
modules.note: Deliberately no claim. No register row says what a deployed API pod or its Service does under this rule, and a result here cannot support one: the suite involves no runtime process, no kubelet, and no Service.

modules.protects: What the API refuses about a request body, the rule that a refusal names the member and never the value beside it, and the validation of a caller-supplied request or correlation identifier - which is echoed in a response header, so a newline in one is a header injection rather than an identifier.

The local cluster and release lifecycle scripts against the safety and ownership rules ADR 0001 and ADR 0004 state for them: every deletion names the cluster or is namespaced and label-scoped, no kubectl or helm invocation can inherit an ambient kubeconfig, every release operation names a namespace, no command passes --create-namespace, nothing prunes the engine or sweeps all namespaces, the read-only scripts stay read-only, every script refuses an argument it does not understand, the host thresholds and the node-image pin are the documented ones wherever they are written, and every workflow that reports release residue asks inside a bounded retry rather than once, so a pod the garbage collector has not yet removed is not reported as residue.
modules.note: No published claim covers it. The claims that a local cluster is created and removed without residue, and that a Helm release installs and uninstalls without residue, belong to the smoke layers, which run against a real engine; this suite reads the scripts as text and could not support either claim if it named them. It defends the properties that make a runtime result reproducible rather than the result itself.

modules.protects: Every module under src/inferops/ is read for its imports, and the platform domain acquiring a Kubernetes client, a Helm library, a runtime SDK, or an HTTP framework is a failure.
modules.note: No published claim covers the dependency rule. It is an architecture decision rather than a claim about the product, and the claim matrix names none — but the rule is what makes the unit layer possible at all, so the check is here rather than deferred until a claim needs it.

modules.protects: The Helm chart against the ownership inventory and the accepted pins: that it renders only what Helm is allowed to own and no Terraform-owned object, that every Helm-owned row is either rendered or declared deferred, that the mock and real selection is derived from the profile in one place the values contract cannot reach, that every image is digest-pinned and every workload carries the six pod and container security fields, that the runtime digest, the model revision, and the runtime arguments still match the records they were copied from, that the probe mapping is the one the accepted health records publish and the runtime liveness probe is a TCP connect rather than the HTTP endpoint that answers 503 while a model loads, that the startup budget covers the largest model load this project has measured, that a termination grace period covers the pause and the drain it has to contain, that no Deployment selector is drawn from anything a values file can change, and that the model cache is mounted at a subdirectory derived from the declared revision with no values path reaching it, with an init container verifying the artifact against the pinned byte count and hash before the runtime is given the same derived path. Since V2-S2-003-PR1 it also renders the V2-generated reference release with its hand-written values and requires the manifests the V1 real values render with the contract's environment label, requires that pair to lint under --strict with no chart guard failing, and measures from lint's report that, given the generated values alone, the chart's guards require exactly four values, each a hand-written row of the V1 synchronous compatibility record and none owned by a contract; since V2-S2-004-PR1 the model's download URL and licence reference are not among them, because the renderer derives both. Since V2-S4-001-PR1 it also requires the API Deployment of both profiles to state the rolling-update strategy the values configure, in whole pods, the schema to take two whole-pod bounds and refuse a percentage, the render to refuse two zero bounds, a second API replica to change one rendered line outside the budget it adds, and both committed renders, which have one replica for each tier, to hold no PodDisruptionBudget. Since V2-S4-002-PR1 it also requires the runtime Deployment of the real profile to state its own strategy, one pod unavailable and no pod above the replica count, the collector alone to state none, each tier's block to require its rollout, the runtime's two zero bounds to be refused under either profile, a runtime replica count or bound outside the schema's range to be refused at render, a second runtime replica to change one rendered line outside the budget it adds, the runtime Service to select every pod the Deployment creates by the Deployment's own selector and to name no replica, no committed values file to add a runtime pod above the replica count, the chart to render no autoscaler, and the desired-state release to render two replicas of each tier from one pod template carrying the pinned image and the pinned artifact, differing from the reference release's render in the two replica lines and in the lines that carry the workload version. One test records a limitation: the chart's schema does not compare a runtime request with its limit. Since V2-S4-002-PR2 it also requires the one runtime pod template of the desired-state release to carry each member of the identity that `tools/runtime_model_cache` expects - the pinned image, one model argument, one read-only claim, the two read-only mounts at the repository-and-revision subdirectory, and the pinned byte count and digest in the verification script - with no environment variable and no host path, the release to render no claim and one writable mount of it, the acquisition hook's, and the three figures of the V1 capacity preflight to be the sums over the release's three Deployments plus one pod with the resources of the chart's release test. Since V2-S4-003-PR2 it also renders the single-runtime baseline profile beside the desired-state release, and since V2-S4-005-PR1 it renders each side with the hand-written values, the release name, and the namespace of its own install description and one placeholder API image digest, and it adds two negative controls, a readiness timeout that changes the rendered readiness probe of the API Deployment, and scrape annotations switched off on one side, which leave the pod templates of that side without the scrape annotation: the two described renders differ in one ConfigMap value, the two configuration checksum annotations, the replica line of the runtime Deployment, and, since chart `0.6.0`, the runtime tier's PodDisruptionBudget, which the target renders and the baseline does not; the API Deployment keeps two replicas, and each probe and each resource request is stated and equal. Since V2-S4-004-PR1 it also requires one `policy/v1` PodDisruptionBudget with `minAvailable: 1` over its Deployment's selector, and with its Deployment's name, labels, and annotations, for a tier of two or more replicas and none at one, none for a runtime that the mock profile does not render, each pod template of the release to be selected by its own budget or by none, no value to configure a budget and the schema to refuse one, no `unhealthyPodEvictionPolicy`, both rollout strategies to stay as the values state them, the inventory row to be `planned` and to cite nothing, the desired-state render's kinds to be exactly the kinds the Argo CD project admits, and the workload policy to accept a render with both budgets. These read a render: no eviction was requested, and no API server admitted a budget.
modules.note: It reads the chart and two committed renders of it. It installs nothing and contacts no cluster, so it says nothing about whether a release installs or uninstalls; that is the kubernetes-smoke layer's question, and the claim it would answer is still a recorded gap. The probe and lifecycle checks it added in V1-S3-002-PR2 are checks on a file: a probe compared against the record that decides it is not a probe that has ever run. The rollout checks it added in V2-S4-001-PR1 are checks on a file too: a stated strategy and a replica count are not a rollout that ran, and they say nothing about what a caller observes when an API pod is unavailable. The checks added in V2-S4-002-PR1 are the same kind: they read a render, and they do not establish that two runtime pods start, that one model cache claim serves both, or that a Service stops routing to a pod that is not Ready. The checks added in V2-S4-002-PR2 read a render and committed figures: they do not establish what a pod mounts or loads, and they measure no host.

modules.protects: The committed ownership inventory against the documents describing it: one owner per resource, and the Terraform and Helm sets disjoint.

The local cluster provider contract ADR 0011 accepted, against its document, the decision record, the ownership inventory, the guard functions in lib.sh, and the Terraform module: exactly two providers, no selection default, Terraform and Helm handed an address and never a provider, an identity check, refusal, or rule claimed as enforced only where the guard or test exists, every capability answer labelled with how it is known and citing a record about that provider, each provider's cluster owned by its operator, no platform workflow that creates or deletes a cluster, and the open gaps pinned so that closing one updates the contract.
modules.note: No published claim covers it. It reads the contract and the scripts as text; that a provider is positively identified, or that a wrong cluster is refused, belongs to test_target_verification.py, which contacts a fake one, or to a layer that contacts a real one.

modules.protects: The Argo CD bootstrap record ADR 0017 accepted, and the procedure that implements it, read as text: that the release is pinned by tag and commit, the install manifest by commit and SHA-256 with a source URL that names the commit and no tag or branch, and each image by digest, and that the pins agree with one another; that the manifest is not copied into the repository; that the object list adds up to the manifest's count, every object maps to an ownership row the argocd-bootstrap owner holds, and every such row is named by the record; that the bootstrap namespace is not the release namespace, the smoke namespace, or Terraform's default, and is outside the inferops- prefix; that a kind the bootstrap shares with Terraform or Helm has a declared boundary and a cluster-scoped kind is shared with no owner; that neither committed chart render and no Terraform file declares a bootstrap-owned cluster-scoped kind or names the namespace; that the two manifests ADR 0019 decided are the only tracked files that declare an Argo CD custom resource, each holds one object, neither is an ApplicationSet, and no file registers a cluster, and the desired-state tree under gitops/ is read and breaks no rule of its own check; that the record says implemented, names one procedure, and cites a committed record for every run and lists every supported provider with no run; that the two procedures and the two manifests are the only tracked files under the build directories that refer to Argo CD, by path or content, under seven spellings the suite matches against its own pattern, and no file under the serving directories does; that every bootstrap row is implemented, names the procedure, and cites a run; that the procedure restates each pin, name, and refusal identifier of the record exactly, lists the 29 namespaced objects and the six containers the record lists, calls the target guard once before its first cluster read, applies the verified file with one server-side apply and edits no object, reads no Secret value, enters no container, and creates no Argo CD custom resource; that the security baseline holds a control for each of the procedure's four guards, three threats, and the two deferred risks; that every rule names a test that exists in this suite or in the executed one, a rule held only by an absence says so, a rule about running the procedure names an executed test and says it runs against stubs, and every refusal names the procedure it applies to; that, in the record's steps, the marker refusal and the first custom-resource refusal precede the first deletion and the definitions are deleted after the controllers stop and after a second check; that the record's page publishes its rules, refusals, removal steps in order, object table, and enforcement split, and the page and the decision publish its pins; and that the architecture index and the ownership document link to the decision and the page. Since V2-S3-004-PR2 one more tracked file matches the custom-resource pattern: the Application as a cluster returned it, in the files of the recorded real-deployment run. The suite names it by its exact path and holds that it is under the proof records, that it is JSON with a status and an object identifier, and that it has the committed Application's name; a second such file fails the test. It does not hold that nothing applies that file.
modules.note: Deliberately no claim: no register row says Argo CD runs, and one provider's run is recorded in a validation record and registers nothing. It establishes that the record is consistent with the ownership inventory, the Terraform defaults, the release namespace constant, the committed renders, and the procedure's own text, and that each pin has the form of an immutable identifier. It reads the procedure and does not run it, so it does not establish that a command does what its text says, that Argo CD installs, reconciles, or can be removed, that upstream still serves the pinned bytes, or that a request is served while Argo CD is absent: it contacts no network and no cluster. One of its checks establishes only an absence. Until ADR 0019 two did; the change that added the first Application replaced one with a test of what that Application may reach, in test_argocd_application.py. It cannot establish that the security baseline rows were written before the first install. It does not check a count that the decision, the index, or the ownership document states in prose. It reads tracked files only, through git ls-files. Until the procedure existed it pinned the opposite state: decided-not-implemented, the manifest not applied, every bootstrap row planned, and no build file naming Argo CD.

modules.protects: The Argo CD bootstrap procedure, by executing it rather than reading it: that a copy of the committed script, run under bash with kubectl, kind, docker, and curl replaced by recording stubs and only the shell's own directory behind them on PATH, makes no kubectl call other than a known read when no provider is selected, the provider is unsupported, a kind target has no cluster name, or the reachable cluster is not the selected one, for each of install, verify, and remove, and does not read the installation before the target is verified; that install refuses an untested or unreadable Kubernetes minor, a namespace without the bootstrap marker, each of the five cluster-scoped objects when no marked namespace exists, an installation that records another pin, a namespace that carries the label and records no SHA-256, a namespace that is being deleted, manifest bytes that are not the pin whether supplied or downloaded, a failed download, a missing manifest path, and an unanswered query; that remove runs nothing without confirmation, refuses an absent or unmarked namespace and one being deleted, refuses while an Application, an ApplicationSet, or an AppProject exists, refuses again when one appears after the controllers stop and then deletes no definition, role, binding, or namespace, does not read an unanswered query as absence, a pod query included, deletes no definition while a pod remains, reports success only after it sees the namespace gone, bounds every deletion, removes an installation with an older pin, and does not query a definition that no longer exists; that a removal makes exactly ten deletions, each of a named object, in the order the decision gives, through the pinned kubeconfig and context, and nothing in another namespace; that verify passes on the pinned installation and changes nothing, fails on another digest, the other image's digest, a missing container, an unlisted container, and a container with no image identity, and fails on an absent, unmarked, or differently pinned namespace and a missing object; that, with sha256sum also replaced by a stub that reports the pin, a first install creates the namespace with its label and its recorded SHA-256 in one request and then applies with server-side apply and the field manager, a second install applies and creates nothing, another object count or a container away from its pin withholds success, and a manifest that changes after its check is not applied; and that an argument the procedure does not understand, an empty manifest path and a repeated one included, runs nothing.
modules.note: Deliberately no claim: every external tool is a stub, so this is substituted execution, and no register row says Argo CD runs. It can distinguish a refusal that fires from one that is written down, which the static suite cannot. One control case establishes that the sandbox reaches the deletions, so the negative results are not vacuous. A test cannot hold bytes with the pinned SHA-256, because the manifest is not committed, so the tests of the path after the digest check replace sha256sum as well; the first version of this module had none, and its negative assertions listed eight mutating verbs where it now lists the known reads. Its curl stub is a shell script and did not reproduce the path defect that the first run on Windows exposed. It does not reach a time limit. It contacts no cluster and no network. It skips, loudly, where bash is absent.

modules.protects: The one Argo CD Application and its project that ADR 0019 decided, and the procedure that applies them, read as files: that each manifest is one marked object in the namespace argocd with no finalizer and no annotation; that one desired-state release is declared and the Application's name and values path are derived from it; that its source is the chart at the revision main names, with one source and the release name lib.sh declares; that its destination is the namespace the binding names, and not argocd; that its sync policy is automated sync with self-heal and without pruning and nothing else; that its hand-written values pass the admission check, share no path with the committed generated values, carry no API image digest, and equal the admitted fixture without its digest; that the project admits one repository, one destination, no cluster-scoped kind, and exactly the eight kinds the committed real render holds without the helm test pod, and PodDisruptionBudget, which that render does not hold at one replica for each tier; that no admitted kind is one Terraform owns; that no rollout or analysis object is committed; that the ownership inventory gives the two objects one owner that names the procedure; that the procedure restates the manifests' names, asks for every admitted kind when it looks for residue, mutates with the four commands it documents and no other, forces nothing, deletes no namespace and no claim, reads no Secret value, sends every kubectl call through the target wrapper, and prints that its report is not a caller outcome; and that the document publishes every refusal the procedure states.
modules.note: Deliberately no claim: no register row says Argo CD reconciles a release, and one provider's run is recorded in a run record and registers nothing. It reads files, so it does not establish that Argo CD accepts the manifests, that a sync succeeds, that self-heal reverts a change, that a removal deletes the workload, or that the workload serves a request. It does not render the chart: the kinds it compares are those of the committed render of the real profile, and not of a render with the Application's own values, so a chart change that adds a kind only under those values passes here. The chart suite renders the desired-state release, where Helm is installed, and compares its kinds with the project. It restricts one Application and says nothing about the controller's grant or about an object a person creates in a cluster. It contacts no cluster and no network.

modules.protects: The Argo CD Application procedure, by executing it rather than reading it: that a copy of the committed script and manifests, run under bash with kubectl, kind, docker, and sleep replaced by recording stubs, makes no kubectl call when no provider is selected and no mutation on a cluster that is not the selected one, for each of apply, verify, and remove; that apply refuses without a well-formed API image digest before any call; that every operation refuses an Argo CD the bootstrap did not install; that apply refuses a destination without the claim or one it cannot read, a recorded Helm release, and any Application, ApplicationSet, or AppProject it did not create, an unmarked object of its own name included, and does not read an unanswered query as an absence; that apply patches each manifest locally, applies the project and then the Application with one field manager and no force, adds the recorded SHA-256 to both and the digest parameter to the Application only, builds both documents before it applies either and applies nothing when one cannot be read, waits until the operation succeeded at the compared revision for the digest it was given, does not accept a comparison from before the apply, and fails when the whole spec or the recorded SHA-256 of a live object is not the committed one; that verify changes nothing, refuses beside a foreign object, and fails on the same differences; and that remove needs confirmation, refuses while the application controller is not ready or the live Application names another destination, adds the finalizer and deletes the Application before it asks for residue, deletes the project only after the residue question returned nothing, keeps the project when it cannot ask, fails when a claim is gone afterwards, and touches only the two named objects; and that observe makes no call without a selected and verified target, reads nothing without a stated count, interval, and name within their bounds, refuses a directory that exists before any call and leaves it as it was, reads the Application as JSON and the release objects the stated number of times with one wait between two samples and no mutation, writes a header, three files for each sample, and an end file, records a read that did not answer as unanswered without keeping its output and goes on, treats an absent Application as an observation, and writes a directory from which the evidence tool builds a complete record.
modules.note: Deliberately no claim: kubectl, kind, docker, and sleep are stubs, so this is substituted execution, and no register row says Argo CD reconciles a release. The stub answers what a test tells it to answer, so it does not establish that Argo CD syncs, that a cascade deletes a workload, or what a real API server returns. Two control cases establish that the sandbox reaches the two applies and the deletions, so the negative results are not vacuous. The wait for a new comparison after a changed Application is executed here only: no run on a cluster applied a second digest. It does not reach a time limit, and it does not execute the diagnostics path. Two runs on one provider executed the operation with the real tools. It contacts no cluster and no network. It skips, loudly, where bash is absent.

modules.protects: The collector of the V2 capacity gate, `scripts/environment/capacity-preflight.sh`, read as text and executed: that each kubectl call the script holds goes through one function and is a `get` or a `version`, that it calls no helm, that its two docker calls read the engine, and that its two removals name files of its own directory; that the schema, the module, the refusal exit status, and each file name it restates are the tool's; that the footprint is written after the target is verified and before the first collected read; and, with kubectl, kind, docker, and git replaced by recording stubs, that an accepted reading writes each read and the record the tool gives for the directory and makes no kubectl call that is not a known read, that a refused reading exits 5 and keeps the directory, that a read that does not answer writes no file and refuses as ambiguous, that an engine that does not answer leaves no engine figure, that an earlier directory is not written into, and that a name outside the collections directory, no provider, a working tree without a commit, and a working tree that differs from its commit each end the run before a list is collected.
modules.note: Deliberately no claim: kubectl, kind, docker, and git are stubs, so the executed tests are substituted execution, and no register row says that a cluster can hold the two-replica release. The stub answers what a test tells it to answer, so the suite does not establish what a real API server returns, or that the collector works on a provider. modules.protects: The collector of the endpoint-state record, `scripts/environment/service-endpoint-state.sh`, read as text and executed: that each kubectl call the script holds goes through one function and is a `get`, that it calls no helm, that it holds no request, no forwarded port, and no process inside a pod, and that its two removals name files of its own directory; that the schema, the module, the refusal exit status, and each file name it restates are the tool's; that the two instants bracket the two reads, and that the header names the provider and no kubeconfig context; and, with kubectl, kind, docker, and git replaced by recording stubs, that an observed reading writes each read and the record the tool gives for the directory and makes no kubectl call that is not a known read, that a reading with no Ready endpoint exits 0, that a read that does not answer writes no file and exits 5 with no count stated, that an earlier directory is not written into, and that arguments that are not usable, no provider, and a working tree without a commit each end the run before a list is collected.
modules.note: Deliberately no claim: kubectl, kind, docker, and git are stubs, so the executed tests are substituted execution, and no register row says that a Service had a Ready endpoint. The stub answers what a test tells it to answer, so this establishes what the script asks and writes, and not what an API server returns.

modules.protects: The provider-aware target guard in lib.sh (inferops::resolve_target and the functions it calls), executed rather than read: every one of the nine documented refusals that a fake kubectl/kind/docker can exercise, for both kind and docker-desktop, a positive verified case for each provider, the target facts a verified run reports, and the capability refusal api-image.sh and model-seed-image.sh depend on to refuse loading an image into Docker Desktop. The guard is driven with no INFEROPS_ variable inherited from the operator's shell, and one test exports a selection to show it does not reach the refusals.
modules.note: No published claim covers it. It contacts no real cluster -- kubectl, kind, and docker are fake executables answering from environment variables -- so it establishes that the guard's own logic refuses and verifies correctly, not that a real cluster is identified or a real wrong one is refused; that belongs to a layer that contacts one.

modules.protects: The Terraform prerequisite layer against the ownership inventory: that every resource the configuration declares maps to a Terraform-owned row and every Terraform-owned row in scope is declared, that the declared kinds are exactly the two expected ones so a new kind cannot arrive unnoticed, that no release object, derived object, deferred row, second provider, or cluster-creating resource appears, that the namespace and the claim carry the project label and the prerequisite lifecycle marker a scoped sweep must exclude, that the namespace is the one the release lifecycle installs into and is not the one another script deletes outright, that the claim name is the one the chart mounts and the default size covers two copies of the pinned artifact, that the provider pin is exact and identical in the module, the environment, and a lock file covering six platforms, that the provider names its kubeconfig and context rather than inheriting them and no host path or credential is committed, that an apply cannot hang waiting for a binding that needs a pod, and that state and plans are ignored by version control while the lock file is not.
modules.note: It reads four small Terraform files, a lock file, a wrapper script, and the ownership inventory. It applies nothing and contacts no cluster, so it says nothing about whether this configuration provisions a namespace or a claim; every Terraform row in the inventory is still planned for that reason. The format and validation checks it delegates to the terraform binary skip, loudly, where the binary is absent.

modules.protects: The prerequisite teardown's release guard, by executing it rather than reading it: that a copy of the committed wrapper, run under bash with terraform, kubectl, docker and helm replaced by recording stubs and no other command on PATH, reaches terraform destroy only when a successful release listing established that the namespace holds none, and refuses -- invoking no destroy at all -- when a release is installed, when another party's release is installed, when helm is absent from PATH, when the listing fails on authorization, transport or an unreadable release record, when the listing returns output that is not a release name, when a release is present in a non-deployed state that only --all reports, when confirmation is missing, and when the reachable cluster is not the one this project created.
modules.note: It runs the committed shell, so unlike its sibling module it can distinguish a refusal that fires from a refusal that is only written down: the guard it covers passed a string-matching test while treating every failed Helm query as proof that no release was installed.
